newsitem.title: USA: NYS Parks Commissioner says Congress favors West.
newsitem.headline: NYS Parks Commissioner says Congress favors West.

text.p: New York State Parks Commissioner on Tuesday said that the way Congress divides up a huge federal fund for parks favored rural, western states, a policy that hurt states in the East.

At the same time, Gov George Pataki urged Congress to fully restore funds for states under the Federal Land and Water Conservation Fund, and attacked President Bill Clinton's plans for the fund in his budget for 1998.

"While we applaud the recent news that the 1998 budget resolution will increase funding for the Federal Land and Water Conservation Fund, we are dismayed that none of this new funding has been earmarked for the state side of the program," he said, in prepared remarks.

The New York State Republican governor said the fund was authorized at $900 million a year with revenues that mainly stemmed from royalities on federal offshore oil and gas leases but in recent years, the program has not been fully funded even though the nation got nearly $4 billion from offshore oil and gas proceeds. He added that in 1996, Congress appropriated only $138 million for the fund, which has led to a $11 billion backlog of state and federal projects.
In New York State, the federal monies have been used for outdoor recreation projects, like urban basketball courts and softball fields.

Castro, who made her comments in prepared remarks, planned to testify on Wednesday before the U.S. Senate's Energy and Natural Resources Committee. "The Land and Water Conservation Fund has lost its balance," she said.
